properties.description: Metadata-driven Bronze ingestion. Reads ctl.source_config, loops it, runs 01_bronze_ingest once per source, and logs every step to ctl.pipeline_run_log. Adding a source means inserting a row in ctl.source_config - this pipeline does not change.

batch_id.description: Overridden by the schedule trigger. Left empty when run by hand, in which case the first activity generates one.

source_system_filter.description: Optional. Set to a single source system name to re-run just that feed after a failure, instead of the whole batch.

activities.name: Set batch id
activities.description: One identifier for the whole run. Every Bronze row written by this pipeline carries it, which is what makes a re-run able to reclaim and replace its own rows instead of duplicating them.

activities.name: Start batch
activities.description: Opens the batch-level row in ctl.pipeline_run_log so there is something to look at while the run is still in progress.

activities.name: Read source config
activities.description: THE metadata-driven step. Everything this pipeline does afterwards is decided by these rows, not by its own structure. load_order puts master data ahead of the transactions that reference it, so referential DQ rules are not firing on the first run for reasons that have nothing to do with data quality.

sqlReaderQuery.value: SELECT source_id, source_system, entity, target_table, file_pattern, is_date_partitioned, file_format, delimiter, decimal_mark, encoding, has_header, sheet_name, load_type, watermark_column, watermark_value, key_columns FROM ctl.source_config WHERE is_active = 1 AND ('@{pipeline().parameters.source_system_filter}' = '' OR source_system = '@{pipeline().parameters.source_system_filter}') ORDER BY load_order;

activities.name: Log step start
activities.description: Returns the run_id that the end-of-step activities update.

activities.name: Run bronze notebook
activities.description: The whole config row is passed as one JSON parameter rather than as seventeen. One parameter that is always in sync with ctl.source_config beats seventeen that can drift out of it, and adding a column to that table then costs nothing here.

activities.name: Log step success
activities.description: Parses the notebook's exit value and records the counts. rows_read and rows_written must match in Bronze - the reconciliation view surfaces any gap rather than letting it be discovered three layers downstream.

text.value: EXEC ctl.usp_log_step_end @run_id = @{activity('Log step start').output.resultSets[0].rows[0].run_id}, @status = '@{json(activity('Run bronze notebook').output.result.exitValue).status}', @rows_read = @{json(activity('Run bronze notebook').output.result.exitValue).rows_read}, @rows_written = @{json(activity('Run bronze notebook').output.result.exitValue).rows_written}, @rows_rejected = @{json(activity('Run bronze notebook').output.result.exitValue).rows_rejected}, @files_read = @{json(activity('Run bronze notebook').output.result.exitValue).files_read};

activities.name: Advance watermark
activities.description: Runs only after the load has succeeded AND been logged. A crash anywhere earlier leaves the old watermark, so the next run re-reads the same window - which is harmless, because Bronze deletes its own batch before appending. Skipping would lose rows permanently. Always prefer duplicated work over lost data.

activities.name: Log step failure
activities.description: The failure path. Records the error against the same run_id so the batch reconciliation shows which source failed and why, rather than just a shorter list of successes.

activities.name: End batch
activities.description: Closes the batch row and rolls up its children's counts. Depends on Completed rather than Succeeded so the batch is closed even when a source failed - an eternally RUNNING batch row is worse than a FAILED one.
